title: Sunny and the Seed Puffs | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka blows a fluffy seed puff in the moonlight and watches it drift away on a tiny adventure through the quiet bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny spotted the first one drifting past her nose at dusk.

A seed puff — a tiny globe of white fluff, floating on the evening air as if it weighed nothing at all. Because it did weigh nothing at all.

She reached out a paw. It drifted just past her. She watched it float away, soft and bright as a tiny star.

Then she found the plant it had come from — a tall stem crowned with a perfect white globe, dozens of seeds arranged around a single centre. All of them waiting.

Sunny leaned close. She pursed her lips and blew.

Very softly.

The seeds flew. Up, and sideways, and apart — each one a tiny white parachute catching the night air and floating away on its own small journey.

She watched them go. One drifted toward the creek. One rose up past the trees. One settled very slowly on the surface of a leaf, rested there for a moment, then lifted again.

Every one was going somewhere different. Every one was so light, so free.

Sunny blew on another globe. Then another. The air around her filled with tiny floating seeds, all drifting, all finding their own quiet way through the dark bush.

She sat down in the grass and watched them disappear — one by one — into the night.

And she thought: I hope they all find good places to grow.

She lay back in the soft grass, the last few seeds drifting above her, and closed her eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, seed puffs. Goodnight, little one.
